source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Decide whether a hot-or-cold judgement can rely on touch or must be checked by measuring temperature.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The same water will feel warm to one hand and cold to the other even after both hands were kept in the same cold water.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Even after their readings settle, thermometers previously in hot and cold water will give different readings in the same water.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: The red water is hotter than the blue water even though both thermometers show the same temperature.

intelligence.enrichment: Sense of touch cannot always decide correctly whether a body is hot or cold; temperature is the reliable measure of hotness or coldness. Different prior contact can change what the same water feels like, while a temperature measurement gives the dependable comparison. The learner correctly applies this rule: Sense of touch cannot always decide correctly whether a body is hot or cold; temperature is the reliable measure of hotness or coldness. If water or a forehead feels hot to a hand, it is hot and no thermometer is needed.
